reason: e32-soak-r2-e29 was stopped after 63 seconds by the harness's planning guard, not by the cluster: 73 accepted mutations in one rolling second against a planning rate of 72/s, during player registration. No tile lost its lease, through barriers of up to 896 ms. That row stays failed. This is the one named retry, with the guard checking the budget it stands for.

planning_guard.what_it_protects: The store keeps the last 9,216 mutation receipts so a retried command gets its original answer. The longest client retry budget is 27 s (3 attempts of 3 s connect, 3 s write, 3 s read). E24 requires the cap to hold four times the mutations of one retry budget: 1 + 4 * ceil(27 * rate) <= cap.

observed_on_this_host.run: e32-soak-r2-e29, store seconds 1 to 63: startup and registration only
observed_on_this_host.loaded_window: not reached; this retry reports it

observed_on_the_workstation.run: e28-soak-r2, standard store with renewals journaled at about 16/s

planning_guard.why_the_one_second_check_misfires_here: Registration commits as fast as the store's barrier lets it, about 70 to 100 a second on this disk, and commits bunch behind barrier stalls. The 72/s figure was E24's measured workload rate plus an allowance. It was never the cap's limit. A one-second burst does not fill a window that is sized for 27 seconds.
planning_guard.conclusion: The registration burst does not threaten the receipt window on this host. The guard for this retry is the budget itself: at most 27 * 85 = 2295 accepted mutations in any rolling 27 seconds, checked live over the whole store trace. The cap, the retry budget and the 4x margin are unchanged.
planning_guard.readback_unchanged: The loaded-window readback still requires at most 72 mutations in any second and cap >= 1 + 4 * max(27 * one-second peak, 27-second peak).
